answers.answer: Matches DwarfStar's 128 GB route: Q2 with SSD streaming (September weights)
answers.conditions: DwarfStar runs its Q2 file (365.7 GB) on one 128 GB Mac by streaming routed experts from SSD (--ssd-streaming), with the expert cache sized automatically. DwarfStar publishes no V4.1 speed for a 128 GB Mac (its one Mac figure is Q4 resident on a 512 GB M3 Ultra). Two 128 GB machines can instead hold it resident with tensor parallelism (set machines to two). Image input works on Metal with its separate 0.97 GB vision encoder. DwarfStar is a community engine, not DeepSeek's code; these are its documented setups, not a RigCheck estimate. Keep the GGUF on a fast local SSD (the 188.83 GiB of Engram tables are always read from the file).

answers.answer: Experimental: DwarfStar's September setup applied to its 1017 file: Q2 with SSD streaming (1017 weights)
answers.conditions: DwarfStar runs its Q2 file (365.7 GB) on one 128 GB Mac by streaming routed experts from SSD (--ssd-streaming), with the expert cache sized automatically. Two 128 GB machines can instead hold it resident with tensor parallelism (set machines to two). DwarfStar documents and tests these setups with its September file only. On October 19, 2026 it published DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-IQ2_XXS-Q2_K-imatrix.gguf (365.7 GB, the size of its September Q2; its name gives the same IQ2_XXS / Q2_K mix) and pointed its Q2 download target at it, whose help text names SSD streaming on one 128 GB Mac, tensor parallelism on two, or a larger resident Mac. RigCheck applies the September setup to it. No 1017 speed or 1017 Q4 file is published; its 1017 MXFP4-experts GGUF (501.6 GB) has no documented setup. DwarfStar's vision encoder is from the September checkpoint; it does not say whether it works with the 1017 file. DwarfStar is a community engine, not DeepSeek's code; these setups are documented for its September file, not a RigCheck estimate. Keep the GGUF on a fast local SSD (the 188.83 GiB of Engram tables are always read from the file). Experimental alternative for 1017: Unsloth says its UD-IQ1_S GGUF (233.0 GB; its 110.6 GB Engram table stays on SSD via mmap) works on 128 GB RAM setups such as a MacBook, DGX Spark or RTX Spark, and estimates 128–145 GB of RAM plus VRAM for its 1-bit builds, the top of a 128 GB machine (runtime and context can need more); it runs only in Unsloth's unmerged llama.cpp pull request #30817 branch or Unsloth Desktop, with no published speed.

answers.answer: Matches DwarfStar: Q2 or Q4 fully resident on a 512 GB Mac (September weights)
answers.conditions: DwarfStar names a 512 GB Mac as the resident target for its Q4 file (518.6 GB in two parts; 294.15 GiB of main weights) and says full residency was tested on an M3 Ultra with 512 GB. Its Q2 file (151.77 GiB of main weights) also fits resident on any 256 GB or larger Mac. DwarfStar's QA record for Q4 fully resident on a 512 GB M3 Ultra (36,864-token allocation, medians of three sweeps): 341.75 tokens/s prefill and 18.69 tokens/s generation at a 4,096-token context, 18.11 tokens/s generation at 32,768. That is the only published Mac speed for V4.1: M3 Ultra with Q4, none for Q2 or the M5 Ultra. Image input works on Metal with its separate 0.97 GB vision encoder. DwarfStar is a community engine, not DeepSeek's code; these are its documented setups, not a RigCheck estimate. Keep the GGUF on a fast local SSD (the 188.83 GiB of Engram tables are always read from the file).
